num__ObstructiveApneaIndex.label: Plausible
num__ObstructiveApneaIndex.reason: More obstructive apneas increase sleep fragmentation and hypoxemia, which can elevate subjective daytime sleepiness. This is a direct mechanistic pathway to higher ESS.

num__SOL_min.label: Plausible

num__T90_pct.label: Plausible
num__T90_pct.reason: Greater time spent with low oxygen saturation reflects sustained nocturnal hypoxemia, which can impair sleep quality and neurocognitive alertness. This can plausibly raise ESS scores.

num__bmi5c.label: Needs caution

num__extrahrs5.label: Plausible
num__extrahrs5.reason: Extra hours (e.g., overtime/extended work or additional time demands) can reduce sleep opportunity and increase sleep debt. Sleep restriction is a strong driver of higher daytime sleepiness.

num__sleepage5c.label: Needs caution
num__sleepage5c.reason: Age is a structural covariate associated with sleep architecture, comorbidities, and sleep-disordered breathing, all related to sleepiness. It is a common confounder but not a modifiable exposure.

num__REM_pct.label: Plausible
num__REM_pct.reason: Altered REM proportion can reflect sleep fragmentation, medication effects, or circadian factors that influence restorative sleep. Changes in REM may plausibly relate to daytime sleepiness.

num__WASO_min.label: Plausible
num__WASO_min.reason: More wake after sleep onset indicates fragmented sleep and reduced consolidated sleep time. Fragmentation commonly increases subjective daytime sleepiness.

num__SDNN_ms.label: Plausible

num__StageShiftIndex.label: Plausible

num__N3_pct.label: Plausible

num__ArousalIndex.label: Plausible

num__AwakeningIndex.label: Plausible

num__MeanRR_ms.label: Plausible
num__MeanRR_ms.reason: Mean RR (inverse of heart rate) reflects autonomic tone during sleep and can shift with arousals and sleep quality. Autonomic dysregulation is plausibly linked to nonrestorative sleep and sleepiness, though confounding is possible.

num__MeanSpO2.label: Plausible
num__MeanSpO2.reason: Lower mean nocturnal oxygen saturation indicates greater hypoxemic burden, which can impair sleep quality and daytime alertness. This provides a plausible pathway to higher ESS.

num__N1_pct.label: Plausible
num__N1_pct.reason: Higher N1 proportion often reflects lighter, more fragmented sleep and reduced restorative depth. Lighter sleep can plausibly increase daytime sleepiness.

num__N2_pct.label: Plausible
num__N2_pct.reason: Shifts in N2 proportion can reflect altered sleep architecture due to fragmentation, medications, or sleep disorders. Such architectural changes can plausibly relate to daytime sleepiness.

num__RMSSD_ms.label: Plausible

num__SWA_Decline_Ratio.label: Plausible
